item.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 Makes History Reaching One Light-Day From Earth
item.description: NASA’s Voyager 1 probe, humanity’s farthest-flying spacecraft, has reached one light-day from Earth, after more than 49 years of constant travel. A light-day is the distance light travels in 24 hours, equaling about 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers).

item.title: Accelerating Quantum Error Correction Simulations under Coherent Noise with Compiled Clifford-Augmented Matrix Product States
item.description: Reliable assessment of quantum error correction requires understanding how coherent errors affect logical performance. Although tensor networks naturally capture coherent interference, entanglement growth and large qubit counts make repeated sampling costly.

item.title: Guarding the Kingdom of Skill-Based Agents in the AI Dynasty of Computation: Control-Flow Integrity for Agent Skills
item.description: Control-flow integrity (CFI) confines a program to a control-flow graph fixed ahead of time. Procedural agent skills move this control flow into prompt text, and a large language model (LLM) agent decides at runtime whether each step runs in its reasoning, a tool call, or a script.

item.title: Movement Information from a Robotic Effector Influences Human Performance During Object Handovers
item.description: Recent advances in robotics have increased opportunities for humans and robots to collaborate during object manipulation tasks. Effective coordination in such interactions depends on how humans use movement information provided by a robotic partner to organize and adjust their own actions.

item.title: Fault-tolerant quantum processor with minimal external control
item.description: Contemporary classical information processors integrate tens of billions of transistors printed on a chip, yet are fully controlled through comparatively few external wires. This is possible because data flows through hard-coded operations in step with a global clock and is steered by external instructions.

item.title: Weight-Space Programming Doesn't Need Transformers
item.description: Standard neural architectures such as the Transformer were chosen because they train well with gradient descent and run fast on GPUs. In weight-space programming, a large language model (LLM) writes target weights by hand without gradient-based training, so those reasons no longer apply.

item.title: What Does an Agent Need? Bundle-Aware Agent Resource Composition
item.description: An agent resource's value depends on its backbone and companion resources and is known only after execution. Token-based generators remain tied to their training catalog, while independent resource scoring misses complementarities and reused bundles target other tasks.
